chapter: Laine, ragtime bands and the union
title: Joining the musicians' union and his father as an organizer
summary: Lala got into the union free as a hot man, was expelled in 1913 and fined, and recalls the union halls; his father helped organize the union around 1890.

story.theme_name: The musicians' union: cards, locals, and the Black-white merger
story.community_name: The musicians' union: cards, scale and the black-white merger

blocks.x: We called it a ragtime band. But you played mostly for dancing. All dancing, all dancing. We was a place jazz band never went to Union. Yeah. Man, when they got us they put us in there for nothing just so they'd have hot men in the band in the Union. We got in there for nothing. We didn't pay no dues or no initiation or nothing like that. How much did it go now? $50 did it?
Yeah. It was $50, it's gone up to $65 now to get in. Yeah.

We didn't pay in 100. You see I got in in 1913 and I was expelled. I had to put a $200 fine on it. I wasn't paid. Why? You paid my union? Well, everybody didn't put us through. We didn't get all the jobs down there. We didn't play. All the balls and all that. We didn't play with all these young fellas that were there. We didn't play. They were working in the Union there and they'd get the jobs too. And after that they took me back with Hill. See? They took me back. Jacked up at the one. Fixed it all up. I remember the union was on Rock Street. I guess it was on Rock Street. That time I'm talking about the, you know what the union was? No. Exchange Alley. Exchange Alley. Exchange Alley between Canal and Iverville. That's Iverville. That's Iverville. There's one in that boardroom. Oh. Exchange Alley. You don't have one that was on Rock Street. Oh yeah. 205 Royal. I belong to him. Well when they sold that building now. I got $500, my daddy got $500. We were stockholders in that building. Your daddy played music? My daddy was one of the organizers of the Musicians Union. 205. Trumpet. My daddy, if my daddy had been living, a few years back when they gave all these old bullets, like Santa Troops and all them, they all got all the organizers of the Musicians Union. My daddy was one of the organizers.
When did the union start up? About what year?
About 19, about 18. It was local there, no office? Started in the 18 hours? About 1890, something like that. Oh. I didn't realize it was that old. Yeah. About 1890. It was local here in this city.
